# Proof page (`PROOF.md`): what it is and how it is regenerated

Status as of 2026-09-10: the tool ships in the package
(`bijotel.tools.proof_stats`, since this commit); the cron described below is
**not deployed yet**. The `PROOF.md` at the repo root was generated by hand
on 2026-09-10 with the manual procedure at the end of this page, from the
three JSON snapshots kept under `tests/fixtures/proof/`.

## What the page is

`PROOF.md` is a Markdown snapshot of the two production chains (GENA, ARA)
and of the federation cross-anchors. It is produced by two read-only steps:

1. `collect` -- opens a chain DB and/or a federation DB with SQLite
   `?mode=ro` and prints one JSON object (counts, seq range, first/last
   entry time, days running, head age, a keyless link check over the last N
   rows, seq gaps, entries per UTC day for the last 7 days; for the
   federation: operators, submissions, anchors, Rekor log indexes).
2. `render` -- turns one or more of those JSON files into the Markdown page.

Every number on the page is as-of the `measured_at_utc` of the JSON it came
from (also printed in the tables). Nothing on the page is live; a reader who
wants the current state must regenerate it or query the hosts.

## The tool

```
python -m bijotel.tools.proof_stats collect --chain <chain.db> [--federation <federation.db>] \
    [--label GENA] [--link-n 1000] [--now 2026-09-10T12:00:00Z]      # JSON on stdout
python -m bijotel.tools.proof_stats render gena.json ara.json federation.json \
    [--generated-by manual|cron] -o PROOF.md
```

Properties (all tested in `tests/test_proof_stats.py`):

- **Read-only.** Every SQLite open is a `file:...?mode=ro` URI; a write
  attempt fails with "attempt to write a readonly database". The tool never
  creates, restarts or writes anything on the host it runs on.
- **Stdlib only.** The module has no third-party imports, so its source can
  be fed to a bare `python3` (host or container). `bijotel` itself is
  imported lazily and only for its version; on a host without the package the
  JSON simply carries `"bijotel_version": null` (this is the case for the
  federation snapshot, taken with the ARA host python).
- **No network.** The Rekor URL is copied from `cross_anchors.rekor_url` as
  stored by the federation service; the tool does not fetch it. Verifying an
  anchor in Rekor is the reader's job (the links on the page).
- **Cheap on a large chain.** The link check reads the last N+1 rows through
  the `seq` primary key and the 7-day histogram scans one integer column.
  On 2026-09-10 the GENA chain (74,773 rows) was collected inside its
  container in a few seconds of wall-clock time including the ssh round
  trip; the collection itself was not timed separately.

- **A check that checked nothing is not a pass.** The link result is
  three-state: valid, broken, or `null` — the last one when there was
  nothing to compare (empty chain, or a window holding no row with a known
  predecessor). The page renders that as `UNCHECKED (n=0, <reason>)`.
  `--link-n` is rejected below 1 for the same reason: a window of zero rows
  would otherwise report a green page for a chain nobody looked at.
- **The footer says how the page was produced.** `render` writes "Generated
  by hand ..." by default and "Regenerated automatically ..." only with
  `--generated-by cron`, so the page never claims automation that is not
  deployed.

What the link check is -- and is not: it verifies `prev_hash(seq) ==
hmac_hash(seq-1)` and `canonical_hash == sha256(canonical_body)` over the
last N rows (N=1000 by default). It does not recompute the HMAC (that needs
the operator secret; use `bijotel verify` for the keyed check) and it says
nothing about rows older than the window.

## Intended setup for S2: one daily cron on the ARA host

The ARA host is the natural place because it already holds all three inputs
without any new data movement:

| Input | Where on the ARA host | Note |
|---|---|---|
| ARA chain | container `ai-research-agency-backend-1`, `/app/data/bijotel_chain.db` | live DB; run the tool inside the container, `bijotel_version` is reported |
| GENA chain | latest `/opt/bijotel-backups/gena_chain_<ts>.db.gz` (pushed daily by GENA through `ops/backup/chain_backup_push.sh`) | a backup, so `head_age_min` and the last-day count reflect the backup time, not the live chain; `bijotel_version` will be null (host python). Confirm the exact file pattern with `ls /opt/bijotel-backups/` before deploying |
| Federation | `/opt/bijotel-federation/data/federation.db` | host python, `?mode=ro` |

Sketch of the job (to live in `ops/` once deployed; **not installed as of
2026-09-10**):

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# proof_page.sh -- read-only; run daily AFTER the 03:45Z cross-anchor and after
# the GENA chain backup has arrived (check both crontabs; 04:30Z is a safe slot).
set -eu
TOOL=/opt/bijotel-proof/proof_stats.py      # copy of src/bijotel/tools/proof_stats.py
WORK=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

# ARA chain: the module is piped on stdin, argv follow the "-".
docker exec -i ai-research-agency-backend-1 python3 - collect \
    --chain /app/data/bijotel_chain.db --label ARA < "$TOOL" > "$WORK/ara.json"

# GENA chain: newest off-host backup, unpacked into the temp dir only.
LATEST=$(ls -1t /opt/bijotel-backups/gena_chain_*.db.gz | head -1)
gunzip -c "$LATEST" > "$WORK/gena_chain.db"
python3 "$TOOL" collect --chain "$WORK/gena_chain.db" --label GENA > "$WORK/gena.json"

# Federation DB, read-only.
python3 "$TOOL" collect --federation /opt/bijotel-federation/data/federation.db \
    --label FEDERATION > "$WORK/federation.json"

python3 "$TOOL" render "$WORK/gena.json" "$WORK/ara.json" "$WORK/federation.json" \
    --generated-by cron -o "$WORK/PROOF.md"

# Publish: commit only PROOF.md into a checkout that uses a deploy key limited
# to this repository. If any step above failed, set -e stopped us here and the
# previous PROOF.md stays in place (never publish a partial page).
cd /opt/bijotel-repo
cp "$WORK/PROOF.md" PROOF.md
git add PROOF.md
git commit -q -m "proof: regenerate $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" && git push -q
```

Variant, per host + rsync: run `collect` on each host for its own live chain
(GENA inside `gena-v4-piata-1` on `/data/bijotel_chain.db`, which also gives
the live head age and the GENA `bijotel_version`), rsync the JSON files to the
host that renders, then render + commit there. More moving parts, fresher
GENA numbers. Either way the render step and the commit are the only writes,
and both happen outside the production data directories.

Operational rules for the job:

- Read-only on the chains and on `federation.db`; never `cp` a live chain DB
  (use the backup or run inside the container), never restart anything.
- The job commits `PROOF.md` only. The JSON snapshots under
  `tests/fixtures/proof/` are test fixtures frozen at 2026-09-10; refresh them
  deliberately, not from cron, or the render tests start depending on the
  day's data.
- Every regeneration replaces the page wholesale; there is no history on the
  page itself. The git log of `PROOF.md` is the history.
- If the page shows `BROKEN` in a link-check cell or `gaps!` in the entries
  cell, that is a finding to investigate, not something to re-run until it
  goes away. `UNCHECKED (n=0, ...)` is also a finding: it means the link
  check compared nothing (an empty chain — e.g. a truncated GENA backup —
  or a window with no row that has a known predecessor), so the cell is
  neither a pass nor a break.
- The job must pass `--generated-by cron` to `render`, otherwise the page
  footer keeps saying it was produced by hand.

## Manual procedure used on 2026-09-10

No package is installed on the hosts, so the module source was sent through
stdin and executed with the host or container `python3`, exactly once per
source, read-only:

```bash
SRC_B64=$(gzip -9c src/bijotel/tools/proof_stats.py | base64 -w0)
PY=$(cat <<PYEOF
import base64, gzip, sys
src = gzip.decompress(base64.b64decode("$SRC_B64")).decode("utf-8")
ns = {"__name__": "proof_stats_inline"}
exec(compile(src, "proof_stats.py", "exec"), ns)
sys.exit(ns["main"](["collect", "--chain", "/data/bijotel_chain.db", "--label", "GENA"]))
PYEOF
)
B64=$(printf '%s' "$PY" | base64 -w0)
ssh -o ConnectTimeout=15 root@GENA_HOST \
    "echo $B64 | base64 -d | docker exec -i gena-v4-piata-1 python3 -" > tests/fixtures/proof/gena.json
# ARA: same with ai-research-agency-backend-1 and /app/data/bijotel_chain.db, label ARA.
# Federation: same on the ARA host without docker, python3 -, with
#   --federation /opt/bijotel-federation/data/federation.db --label FEDERATION
python -m bijotel.tools.proof_stats render tests/fixtures/proof/gena.json \
    tests/fixtures/proof/ara.json tests/fixtures/proof/federation.json -o PROOF.md
```

Measured 2026-09-10 13:53 UTC with this procedure: GENA 74,773 entries
(seq 1..74773, no gaps, link check VALID over seq 73774..74773), ARA 21,784
entries (seq 1..21784, no gaps, VALID over 20785..21784), federation 2
operators, 100 cross-anchors of which 100 carry a Rekor log index, last
